title: THE DEVELOPMENTAL PSYCHOLOGY OF BEING HATED

sense.text:
The scriptures are the solution to our people’s problems, and that is why the Bible is under attack. Don’t keep just one Bible in the house; keep several, because it is going to come under attack. But don’t only have the Bible, read the Bible. There is no point in having a manual you don’t know how to use.

“Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”: you must open the book. A lot of people buy books and never read them. We must read the scriptures.

“no one of these shall fail”. Nothing written in the scriptures is going to fail. That is usually paralleled with prophecy, but it is just as true of the healing the scriptures offer. Cast all your cares upon him, and all the scriptures that deal with mental health: they are true, and they will not fail when they are properly applied. The Bible is the medicine cabinet for our people, and the leaders, as the doctors, go into it to find the medicine for each problem.

Each brother and sister who comes into this truth is special to the Most High. He did not waste his time calling you if he didn’t mean for you to make it.

“The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish”: not willing that any of us should perish. For every one of us that comes into this truth, the desire is for you to make it, and the leadership is here to help you get there.

precepts.why:
“Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure”. You need to understand how special you are. The Most High called the sisters in here and called the brothers in here, and that was not a waste. He made it happen in the heavens when it was time for you to wake up: things were decided in the heavens the day you woke up. Just as there were conversations in heaven about Job, when Satan wanted to tempt him, there are conversations about you repenting. That is love. Understand that sacred calling, and give diligence to make your election a sure election.

Read on: “for if ye do these things, ye shall never fall”. That is the guarantee of keeping God’s commandments, and it means it is up to us. If we get soft and weak and fall out of this truth, we squander the chance we were given to wake up, over some bad habits and temptations, and we lose what Christ promised us: the chance to come out of this and have eternal life.

So see yourself as special. That is how the bishops, the deacons and the whole leadership see each one of the congregation: every one of your spirits is precious to the Most High. It hurts to see a brother or sister get weak in this truth, lose the faith, or feel they can’t make it any longer, and there is no good excuse for not staying steadfast.

“My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” The Lord first selected you and brought you into his marvelous gospel to wake you up and bring you up as princes and princesses. No longer are you to be on the dunghill; you are supposed to come up out of that. Then he tries you, to make sure you are fit for the kingdom.

As you prepare your soul for temptation, that is the Lord trying you to make sure you are worthy of the calling; but it was already discussed in the heavens to bring you in first. So it is up to us to stay diligent and steadfast, and not be pulled off by evil, wickedness, sin and the temptations our people get caught up in. We are a chosen vessel, and we have to see ourselves that way.

sense.text:
A mind is a terrible thing to waste. The mind of the Israelites, men and women, is a precious thing: the Lord called you out of darkness into his marvelous light because you have a mind to do great things. Why give up on yourself and go back to your own vomit? Many came in with good gifts, grew weak hearted, went back into the world, and are doing nothing at all.

Think about our forefathers in chattel slavery, who had nothing near the opportunities we have. They endured years of lynchings, rapes, being tarred and feathered and ripped apart by horses. A husband had to walk out of the slave quarters while the master’s visitors soiled his wife, then come back in with his manhood stepped on; and the wife, after all that, still had to console her husband and make him feel like a man. He did not grab bottles of alcohol and waste away, the way brothers are doing today over their problems. They persevered with no relief in sight, not knowing when emancipation was coming.

“Now faith is the substance of things hoped for”: our people in slavery were hoping for freedom, and faith helped them persevere through tunnels of darkness with no light in sight. Faith is hoping for something that is not in your immediate grasp, not even in your reachable grasp.

“the evidence of things not seen”: the faith in their minds drove them toward something not even in existence yet, and pulled them through all those years without knowing when the end was. Like Joseph in captivity: for nearly 13 to 14 years he did not know he would be brought out, but he knew there is a God, and he stayed until the Lord decided to deal with him.

Some of us committed suicide, it was that bad. But had all of them done it, or all destroyed their livers drinking, we would not be here. They had enough faith to keep pushing through all that evil so that you and I could sit here today. We get a little trouble and suddenly can’t cope and need alcohol and drugs. Joseph didn’t do that, and they couldn’t. We have to put ourselves in discipline.

“And among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest”: that is our brothers and sisters in chattel slavery, and coming up to now. Everywhere we go we are not quite home. We are always being pushed on: move, get from here, you can’t loiter here, you can’t live there. We have never been able to lay our heads down and say, I am home. The only taste of that was coming into this truth and hearing the brothers say, Welcome home, knowing we were on the right ship to take us all home.

“but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart”: wherever we go among these nations, scared, nervous, psychologically wrecked, no solace, no comfort. That is how we lived, and we still live that way. “and failing of eyes”: no hope. You can’t envision how you will end up, a future for your children, where you will be next week, next month, next year. “and sorrow of mind”: sorrow is going through a terrible situation you cannot do anything to change, and having to live through the sorrow of it.

“And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”: in chattel slavery our lives were in doubt every day. Any day we might be killed, any day lynched; not only the mothers and the fathers, but the sons. A mother had to wash the master’s clothes with the blood of her own son in them, the son he lynched for picking up a can that rolled out; and still she could not give up, and the father could not give up.

“and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”: every night in fear, never knowing when they would come in and do what they were going to do. To have no assurance of your life, the way things are looked at today, would be called suicidal. It took a level of faith to make it through those terrible years. So what excuse do we have today?

“In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even! and at even thou shalt say, Would God it were morning!” What carried our sisters and brothers from night to morning and from morning to night, with that uncertainty of life, was faith. They said, we cannot give up now; we have to keep pushing through. They sang in the fields, Swing low, sweet chariot, and believed those spirituals without knowing when it would happen.

“for the fear of thine heart wherewith thou shalt fear, and for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see”: the terror they lived with daily is why they prayed and held on in faith. And they did not even have the truth as we know it. What little they learned, they overheard sitting on the floor in the back of the white man’s lying churches, until brothers like Nat Turner started teaching. Now we know this Bible and we know the future, and we come in here saying, I can’t do this, I can’t do that, and put our heads in a bottle and a crack pipe. That’s crazy.

precepts.why:
Not only were the lives of the mothers and fathers in doubt; the sons were in doubt. “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people”: that could happen at any moment, any day. Your son ripped out of your arms to be sold to some master, and you never see your children again. From the day the child was born until someone said, I want that one as a slave, the parents had nothing to say about it. Imagine that mindset.

“and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long”: our people watched their sons and daughters taken away. And there was no alcohol for them. They had to endure it sober, knowing the Lord was still going to be with them somehow; they could not take themselves out, because a generation was going to come from them, and they kept producing our seed through trauma after trauma.

“and there shall be no might in thine hand”: no might in our hands to stop it. A bottle of whiskey would not have stopped it either.

sense.text:
When you believe you just have to accept this life and suffer peacefully, the psychology you develop is hopelessness and despair: that the order is fixed, as if there is no God. Our forefathers did not feel that way. They chopped off our feet and our hands, and that still did not stop them from pushing on to the point that we were born. Their situations were far worse than my bills, my job, my this and my that; and going to indulge in alcohol as if it will relieve those problems is being a punk.

“Hope deferred maketh the heart sick”: the heart is the mind. Hope deferred makes the mind sick. Hope is supposed to be something attainable. Our people in slavery had hope that we would get out, but many went crazy because they didn’t see it coming. On the ships some dove overboard, taking their babies with them, because they saw no way out; they checked out mentally first. But there was a group, the elite of us, with enough courage in the face of all that ugliness to still reproduce so that we could be here today. That took courage, faith and hope.

Deferred means beyond your grasp, unattainable. When our people come to feel that hope is out of their reach, they shortchange their own aspirations and retreat into nothingness: comfortably numb with mediocrity, unproductiveness, laziness, drugs, alcohol, whoring out their women. They pine away into these things.

“but when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life”: when the hope actually manifests, it makes us glad. We are not supposed to have that deferring, because we are not looking for a nation to save us; we are looking to the Most High, and that is where our faith is. We carry that in our minds even in the face of virulent hatred and extreme violence. Why would you swing the axe and the sword if you don’t have victory in your mind? Because our people don’t believe, they don’t even fight any more, spiritually or psychologically; they say, give me the bottle, I’m nothing. That is a destroyed state of mind. If you see a brother or sister carrying that spirit, it is your job to pull them out of it. We have to be our brother’s keeper and our sister’s keeper.

We are hated, and we know it. When the police went on a rampage against the Muslim brothers in Los Angeles in 1962, the officer asked what the ambulances were rushing for, nothing but some niggers: let them die. Rashan Carter was caught on a deer camera running shirtless for his life, looking back, and his mother Tiffany Carter was handed boxes of her son’s remains with no answers; the people of that town got mad at their own white man for turning the picture in, because they were having fun. Dr. Martin Luther King was not killed by the bullet; the chief of neurosurgery took out his catheters and smothered him with a pillow in the emergency room. That is the climate of hate we live in every day, and it has warped our developmental psychology.

“For, lo, thine enemies make a tumult: and they that hate thee have lifted up the head.” Our enemies hate God and they hate the Israelites. They hate our Father because he chose us to be a special people unto himself above all people on the earth. With that kind of love coming from the Father, what are you doing with your head in a bottle?

“They have taken crafty counsel against thy people”: counsel so crafty we may think we can never get out of this, which is exactly what it is designed to make us think. The hatred, the oppression and the ugly treatment are designed to break black men down, to make them believe the order is fixed and they can only succumb to slavery. If you stand up like men, they get upset; they want you subservient, and if they can’t get that, they will make your life so crazy it drives you to drugs, alcohol, fornication, adultery and every evil that destroys your nation and your family.

“and consulted against thy hidden ones”: gathering together and keeping a plan in place so that we never rise above where they say we should be. Who are they to determine where we should be? We are the hidden ones, God’s people, and they don’t like that. We have to relish being the children of God and act accordingly.

God gave us these bodies, and we are not to abuse them with alcohol, drugs or overeating. Ye are gods, yet we look like something else. As a man thinketh about himself, his body, his family and everything around him will reflect it. Being fat is not normal. The young men of valor have the discipline to separate themselves from the streets and aspire to the tier of men above them; when they look up and see those men going backwards, getting fatter, their aspirations go into reverse. Whatever you are when you come in, get better.

“They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” The way they cut us off from being a nation is to get between you and what is actually going to save you: between you and your salvation, you and righteousness, you and your God, your nation and your family. They will do anything to separate and break you from that.

“For they have consulted together with one consent”: all the nations are in agreement to make sure we stay stupid, stay fat, stay on drugs and alcohol, riotous living, promiscuity, adultery and fornication. Look at the music they give us and the liquor stores all over the place, there for us to drown ourselves in nothingness. Where is the library? Those are plots to keep us destroyed. “they are confederate against thee”.

“The tabernacles of Edom”: the white man, Esau, leading all the rest of the nations. “and the Ishmaelites”: the Arabs, with shops all up in our communities. “of Moab”: the Chinese, all over Africa. Africa has the raw materials, the mines and the gold, yet since the scramble for Africa it has been kept from manufacturing; the colonizers take the materials, sell the goods back at prices the people cannot pay, and lend to them against what grows in their own land through the IMF, until they take over completely. That is the hatred we face all over the world.

“Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek; the Philistines with the inhabitants of Tyre; Assur also is joined with them: they have holpen the children of Lot.” All these nations and many more: that is God’s hit list. They are listed because the Lord is going to go after them specifically.

So what do we do? Walk away from the job of fixing it and go to a bottle, go to drugs? However bleak you think it is, you are still obligated as a man to seek to fix the problem, even without the full answers yet. Seek the answers. Organize, discipline yourself, change your mental state, your conversations and your circle; get with the brothers and sisters who understand the mission. The Most High will intervene and show you the way. The Lord didn’t bring us this far to leave us here.

precepts.why:
All the nations are confederate to destroy us, and Esau leads them. “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel”: this chapter is literally speaking about Esau himself. Perpetual means never-ending. It was created that way from the womb, Esau and Jacob: that spirit was put in them to hate us regardless of anything. “by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end”.

The SPLC is not the only one; all of the nations hate us, and we have to know it and operate in spite of it. It is not for us to loathe ourselves and wallow in it. Let them say what they want: they don’t get to define us. We define ourselves by what God defined us as: the Israelites, the children of the Most High, and we carry ourselves like that.

Our enemies, led by Esau, are making certain that the Israelites stay asleep in ignorance, lies and ultimately sin, and that hatred is rooted deep in their spirit from the womb. Trump is just the hood ornament, the hooded Klansman in our faces, a wake-up call from God to agitate us through oppression.

sense.text:
“Thy sons have fainted”: our sons have fainted because there is no guidance for our children in the streets. “they lie at the head of all the streets”: on the corners with no direction, no aim. Their minds are wasted, and a mind is a terrible thing to waste, especially among our people; our sons are pining away in their iniquities. “as a wild bull in a net”: our young sons in the streets are like wild bulls, gremlins, the new batch.

“they are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God”: full of God’s fury, his judgment, because we broke God’s commandments. Our people are catching hell because God is putting it on them, just as he is putting it on us. That rebuke is not for our destruction. It is to agitate us to organize, to agitate us into keeping God’s commandments and coming together, O nation not desired; that is what it is designed for.

The rebuke is sent on us by God through Esau, because we refuse to return. Why would the Lord put his own people in a climate of hate? To make us ask God, What did we do wrong? And once you recognize what you did wrong, he says, now you’ve got it; let me show you the blueprint to get out of this.

precepts.why:
The rebuke is sent through Esau. “For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain”. If we do evil against the Most High, be afraid. The Most High put this demon over us because we refused to keep his commandments.

Read the verse before: “For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil.” The rulers, the powers that be, are not a terror to those of us who keep God’s commandments. We will still go through persecution and trials and feel all the oppression, but it is not a terror to us, because we know a day of restitution is coming when we will not have to deal with it any more. That is a comfort in our trial and in our captivity.

Our brothers and sisters in slavery needed that same perseverance to pull through all that evil, and we are far better equipped, knowing the Bible as they did not. No matter how hard it gets, there is no death for us in righteousness.

This shows the difference, and it is a comfort we should have. “For I am with thee, saith the Lord, to save thee”: with you, Israel. “though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee”. That whole group read in Psalms 83, the Lord is going to destroy them all; every nation is ultimately going to be destroyed, but not the Israelites. We have been here before and we will be here again: we are in God’s plans to be on this earth forever, if we do what the Lord said. No other nation can claim that. All this is temporary.

The nations whither he scattered us are the very lands where we find no ease and where the sole of our foot can have no rest. He will make a full end of them, but not a full end of the righteous. Some of our own people will be destroyed too, because they will choose the bottle, fornication, debauchery and adultery over the Lord. The ones who stay in righteousness will inherit the kingdom forever and ever. The only reason you would go indulge in sin and a bottle is that you don’t believe; if you believe, you will persevere. And it is not, Lord, will I make it? That is up to you. You find a way to get to the bottle; find a way to make it into the kingdom.

“but I will correct thee in measure”: he will cause us to pass under the rod and teach us his commandments, how to keep them properly. Good days are coming if we stay steadfast in this truth. The oppression is set up to make you believe you cannot escape it, to drive you into insanity, drugs, alcoholism, fornication and adultery, to make you think there is no way out; if you succumb to it, you will be destroyed by it. But the Lord said, Fear not, O Jacob: the Lord is our redeemer.

sense.text:
We are not to keep living in uncertainty, unable to envision a future for ourselves, our families and our nation. We are the guys, and by the power of the Most High and his son Jesus the Christ we build up our weak spots. He said we are a city that sits on a hill.

“Let your light so shine before men”: the Most High is telling us how to operate right now, today. You can’t let your light shine drunk. You can’t let your light shine showing the world you don’t know how to control your eating. Overweight is called that for a reason: special stores, big and tall, two airplane seats. That is not normal; that is abuse. Call it fat shaming if you want: if the shoe fits, wear it, and let it get on your nerves enough to do better. The fat sisters too. If you are comfortable being called overweight, or depending on a chemical to have a good time, something is wrong with you. It is a disease, all of it, and you have the ability to cure yourself. Examine yourself: your conscience, which you try to silence with alcohol, is the part of you that steps outside and says, you’ve got a problem here; when are we going to fix it?

“that they may see your good works”: we are the nation, the stars of God, the trendsetters, meant to set the whole planet in righteousness until the Lord gets rid of them. As Israelites and as IUIC we are that city, that organized nation. The brothers on the corners, the wild bulls in a net, the sister out there half crazy, need to see our good works and ask the reason of our hope; and we tell them, we used to be in your spot, but we repented, and if we can do it, you can do it. Many have lost weight because of the examples set.

This society wants to send our people backwards, with junk food, liquor stores and dope on tap in our communities, because a people with no hope will run to that crutch to drown out the conscience that is chastising them. We have to be better than that and be the example. We can’t leave the post for the fantasy world of video games, grown men wearing gaming diapers so they never get up from the game. That is escapism, the same as the bottle.

Man deals with reality. When we can’t see a future for our families or ourselves, and have no faith to advance beyond where we are, we choose the easier way out rather than challenge what calls for discipline; and it is a betraying comfort to do nothing. Everything IUIC has built, the departments, the missions overseas, the diaspora outreach, the pantries for the famine to come, did not exist at the beginning. It took vision where nothing was yet seen. That is what men do: they prepare. It is no surprise when we do it, because we used the medicine in this Bible and we know the God behind us.

“For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.” Succours means comfort. The fear is the fear of challenging what we don’t want to face. Challenge the weight instead of making excuses for it; challenge your addiction to alcohol instead of finding a scripture to abuse and saying the Bible told me I could. Fear lets you lie that you don’t need real effort, and hands you a betraying comfort to do something else.

It addresses the danger of abandoning logic, and logic is handling the situation in real time. In moments of panic, instead of doing what we are supposed to do, we abandon the logical solution for a fantasy, a betraying lie that says we can get the same result. The answer is no: you have to go through the strait gate to get the real results. Sound judgment is a real effort to correct alcoholic behavior, the discipline to curb the fat you’re building. Running to alcohol, dope, fornication or a video-game woman, instead of getting your finances and yourself together to acquire a real wife, is a betraying comfort, and it ends in destruction.

Reason is what the enemy fears. King Leopold II told the missionaries he sent into the Congo, mercenaries really, to teach the students to read and not to reason: to preach that the poor are happy, to separate the children from their parents, and to make the people despise everything that gives them courage to confront the colonizers. Reasoning is the cognitive process of using existing knowledge and facts to draw conclusions and solve problems; it bridges raw information and rational action. The reasonable solutions are available right around us. That is what the stewardship program was: canvassing the congregation for its doctors, lawyers, nurses, engineers and electricians and organizing them, so that Hope and Healing and the doula program meet real problems with real help. That is not selling out; that is thinking like men.

That is the climate of hate we are up against all over the earth. AfriForum, the descendants of the colonizers of South Africa, ran to Trump, and with Elon Musk pushing, they got all aid to South Africa cut and Julius Malema locked up for five years for the liberation song Kill the Boer, because they need Africa’s resources. This damn devil, the bastard white man, put AIDS over there because he knew he was going to do this later. Their own economist says it plainly: Africa is kept impoverished, by Europe, the US and now China, because they need its raw materials dirt cheap. It is one collective exploitation of us all, from Johannesburg to Harlem, and they keep us divided so a fifth of the world can rule the rest.

Even with that, as insurmountable as it seems, you cannot get weak, succumb to alcohol and say the order is fixed. Get that thinking out of your mind. We have God behind us, and with God behind us there is no doubt. There are bullets out there with our names on them, and if it be the will of the Lord they will use them; but that is not going to stop this. If it happens, I want to die in this, so I can come back and hang my enemies.

Because we don’t reason, we become frustrated and flustered in our thoughts and afraid to point the finger square at the problem. The fear of boldly acknowledging the black Christ, the Saviour of the Holy Bible, and proclaiming that there is no white Christ, makes people say the color of Christ doesn’t matter: a false, betraying comfort that leaves us comfortably numb and unproductive. So, feeling trapped, we resort to the bottle, drugs, promiscuity, prostitution, and violence against those closest to us, mostly against the wife in the home. If our ancestors had used that excuse to get drunk, none of us would be here today.

“Woe unto him that giveth his neighbour drink, that puttest thy bottle to him, and makest him drunken also, that thou mayest look on their nakedness!” Woe to those who press drink on their neighbours and friends and get them drunk, like the chug, chug, chug on the college campuses. The Lord brings destruction on those who do it.

A mother quoted it to her seventeen-year-old son when he stumbled home smelling of drink after a night with his cousins: so your friends put the bottle to your lips. He got so sick, the room spinning, that he vowed never to do it again, and never did.

How often is this verse brought out on alcohol abuse? Hardly at all. The videos on alcoholism get little more than a thousand views, yet excessive drinking costs this economy about 250 billion dollars every year, in lost work, health care and wrecked homes and cars, and it destroys thousands and millions of homes. We live in an alcogenic culture, where the line between social drinking and drunkenness is blurred. No matter how small the problem is among us, it is a bad problem.

Some announce it: I deserve to go out and get drunk, so get out of my way. It is going on in some people’s houses, and a little of it has seeped into the congregations; we see it on the reports as intoxication, and left alone it will get much worse. Getting so drunk you get sick, the body saying don’t take another drink and you taking it anyway, your face in the toilet bowl begging God to get you out of this: that is all-time dumb.

People abuse alcohol to cope with stress, trauma and mental health issues, to blunt their emotions; and over time it goes from a choice to a habit, then an addiction, the brain rewired so the body craves it. A doctor told one of my uncles, if you take another drink you will be dead. We could not mask our emotional pain in slavery, so don’t use that as an excuse; this will kill you. That is why the liquor stores are in our neighborhoods, easy to get and normal on every block. Nobody is drinking measurably or sociably; they are using it to drown out reality. In an alcogenic culture, if you don’t have a cup in your hand you can’t socialize, and those who want to stay sober are pressured. Some of us cannot deal with it at all, and when the reports of drunkenness come, we have to put you out to save the body.

“Thou art filled with shame for glory: drink thou also, and let thy foreskin be uncovered: the cup of the Lord’s right hand shall be turned unto thee, and shameful spewing shall be on thy glory.” Then “the violence of Lebanon shall cover thee”, and on to “What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it”: the chapter goes into idolatry and other things.

So the alcohol lawyers will say it isn’t talking about alcohol at all, only idolatry. But the words are there. Why would the chapter compare the other things in it to the effects of drink, if not for a reason? It has a twofold meaning: while it illuminates the rest of what is going on in the chapter, it is literally talking about alcohol itself.

It is not a sin to drink, but when drinking is used as an outlet for our problems, that is when we fall into damnation and condemnation. That is not the manner it is to be used in. When we are dealing with issues we rely on the scriptures and build our faith to overcome them.

“Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good”: and the good is God’s laws.

precepts.why:
“For if ye live after the flesh, ye shall die”: when we obey the flesh, making the bottle an outlet, death is at the end of that road. As in Habakkuk 2, there is always an evil road, and at its end you find death.

“but if ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live.” Excessive drinking is a quarter-trillion-dollar problem, but the commandments fix all of it. “For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God.” That is how we are to be: not overcome with that evil, but overcoming it with good, which is God’s laws.

“Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart, and cheerfulness of the mind: But wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind”. Measurably. Bitterness of the mind is the key: the Lord can’t use you if you don’t have that balance.

Every element on the earth was created by the Lord and has its function and purpose, but if you use it and abuse it, you can’t be useful for the nation. The same goes for food. Our oppressors are depending on you being out of balance; that is why the KFC sits across the street from the Domino’s. They are counting on you to fall into that destruction, chaos and confusion.

sense.text:
A brother wrote in: his wife of thirty years only supports him when he brings it up and takes no initiative; she doesn’t meal prep or cook even for herself, and he works twelve hours a day and can’t get his lunch packed. He is drained, but she is still his rib. Think of the bus driver who got spat on and went to work on the man: all the twelve-hour days with no sandwich came out at once, and that demon couldn’t be put back in the cage. Brothers, control yourselves and don’t let things take you there; we need you out here, not in jail. But this is the help sisters can give.

“The beauty of a woman cheereth the countenance”: sisters, know your beauty and where your power is. A man needs to be cheered up, and he can do twelve hours if you deal with him right. If a man will go down into a pit and fight lions to bring the spoil home to his wife, as Zerubbabel said in Esdras, what could some kind words do for him? Here’s your sandwich, and he could do twelve more hours. “and a man loveth nothing better.”

“If there be kindness, meekness, and comfort, in her tongue, then is not her husband like other men.” The usual answer is that he has set his house in order, but that is learned response: everyone answering the same way because we only look at it in one direction.

Describe her husband. The wife who does these things turns him into a super god, a superhero; he would be unstoppable. Look what men will do in wickedness: they will sell dope and risk going to jail, five months in and locked up, for a woman who isn’t dealing with them right. What would he do for a woman dealing with him right, in righteousness? She is his comfort, his aid, his cheerleader, on his team, a help meet right for him, and he would have the confidence and fortitude to do anything. He would not be like any of the men we currently see. We can organize this and build that; with that woman in your corner, there is no stopping us.
